PullRequest.Title: agentHost: move_session server tool to move sessions and nested sessions
PullRequest.Body:

Move Chats, Block 6: an agent host server tool, `move_session`, that lets an agent move sessions and nested sessions when the user asks. It is behind `chat.agentHost.moveChats.enabled` (default off), the same setting as the rest of Move Chats, and doesn't depend on the drag-and-drop UI (Block 5).

## What it does

One tool, shaped like `create_session`: `session` (a link; with a `?chat=` id it names a nested session, without one the whole session; omitted means the calling chat), `relationship` (`nested` | `independent`), `into` and `after` (default: at the end). It covers:

- reordering a nested session within its session;
- moving a nested session into another session, after a given nested session or at the end;
- making a nested session its own session (`independent`);
- moving a whole single-chat session into another session.

Moves run on the existing host operations and validation (`AgentService.moveChat` / `moveSession`, the AHP `moveChat` and `vscode/moveSession` paths), in the same move sequencer. The tool's pre-check shares the host's check phases, so it can't drift from them. Every `AgentChatMoveRefusal` maps to one actionable sentence for the model; a compile-time exhaustive map enforces this, including `differentCredentialOwner`.

## Decisions

- **Confirmation:** every call asks the user, reorders included (`sessionConfirmationToolNames`). The prompt is skipped only when the user turned approvals off (Allow All, Claude `bypassPermissions`, Codex full access), as for `create_session` and `delete_session`. The confirmation names what moves and where, linking only sessions and chats the host knows; the host builds it (`IAgentServerToolHost.getConfirmationDisplay`) for Copilot, Claude and Codex.
- **Moving the calling chat:** checked when requested, applied when the turn succeeds, like `set_workspace`. A service plus a turn-end contribution (order 160) do this, and they hold the chat's queued turns until the move is done, so a queued message starts in the new session. A move refused at turn end is only logged.
- **Moving another chat mid-turn:** allowed. The running turn, its pending confirmation and the session status follow the chat; a unit test covers this.
- **Links:** sessions and chats resolve only from links and the sessions' recorded chats; no owner is ever derived from a chat URI.
- **Gating:** `move_session` is in its own non-materialized group that reads the setting on every call and requires the provider's `multipleChats` capability; sessions are re-advertised when the setting changes. With the setting off, `move_session` is absent from every tool list and no description mentions it.
- **General improvement:** `list_sessions` and `get_current_session` now always list a session's main session and nested sessions (`chats`: title, `?chat=` link, `main`, status; list data only). The links work with `send_message`, `get_session_context` and `rename_chat`, and with `move_session` while it is offered.
- **Backstop:** at most 50 moves per process, following the existing orchestration-limits switch.

## Reviews and performance

- Four review rounds. r1 led to the shared pre-checks, held queued turns for a scheduled move, required APIs, the cross-field rules in the schema, and test gaps. r2 was a cleanup. r3 gated the move wording on the setting, sequenced the tool's check and move, and verified the confirmation links. r4: SHIP, with its four LOW findings addressed except the pre-existing Codex `hideConfirmationInput` behavior.
- Performance review: no regression with the setting off. Tool lists are unchanged; the added cost is one config lookup per tool-list query and one `Map.get` per turn end. Each `move_session` call reads the session list once (tool path only).

## Validation

Run on the final commit, rebased onto `e8314212e7d`:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck-client` | passed |
| `npm run eslint -- <30 changed .ts files>` | passed, no warnings |
| Hygiene (pre-commit hook on every commit) | passed |
| `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot` with `sessionServerTools`, `serverToolGroups`, `scheduledChatMoves`, `chatContributions`, `claudeAgent`, `claudeServerToolMcpServer`, `copilotAgentSession`, `copilotToolDisplay`, all 40 `codex/*`, `agentService`, `protocolServerHandler`, `agentHostChatMovability`, `agentSideEffects`, `agentHostContributions`, three telemetry suites, `sessionWorkspaceConversion` | 4877 passing, 19 pending (pre-existing), 0 failing |
| `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/{copilot,claude,codex}AgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep "server tool:\|[Mm]ov"` (strict replay, twice) | Copilot 56 passing + 1 pending; Claude 42 + 8 pending; Codex 51 + 2 pending; both runs green |

- The 18 new `move_session` e2e fixtures (6 tests × 3 providers) were recorded with `AGENT_HOST_REPLAY_RECORD=1`. Later changes produced no cache misses, so nothing was re-recorded.
- The e2e tests cover reorder, move, promote, whole-session move, a self-move applied after `turnComplete`, and a refused move, each with a confirmation shown.
- Azure pipeline 111 (cross-platform Agent Host E2E) is queued after this PR opens.

**Live test** (isolated Code OSS Agents window, Copilot):

- Full run: reorder (approve and deny), move after a given nested session and at the end, promote, whole-session move, moving another chat mid-turn, self-move and self-promote, a queued message running in the new session, refusals, the setting off at launch and flipped at runtime, approvals off, and ownership and order after a restart. All passed.
- Scoped re-run on the fix rounds:
  - discovering nested sessions via `chats` and moving with only those links;
  - move wording off/on with the setting;
  - a promoted session moved as a whole, warm and after a restart;
  - confirmation links (known → link, odd or unknown → plain text, with no injected link or bold);
  - a cold whole-session move, and smoke tests.

  All passed.
- **Not run live:** Claude and Codex (their SDKs write to the real home directories, so they can't be isolated); both are covered by the e2e tests. Also not run: `differentCredentialOwner` (no sponsored session in isolation; unit-covered on the host side).

## Follow-ups

- Called from a non-top-level chat (for example a HydraFusion solver), `move_session` gets the Copilot harness's generic "This tool can only be called from a top-level chat with a known root tool-call origin." That message is shared by every `topLevelChatOnly` tool; making it actionable is a harness change.
- With the setting off, a session that advertised the tool earlier gets the framework's generic "Server tool … is disabled." A group-specific message needs an `IServerToolGroup` hook.
- Editor tabs aren't reordered live after a reorder (sidebar and database are correct).
- Codex ignores `hideConfirmationInput` for server tools (pre-existing).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path, cache lifetime, I/O boundaries, and all-sessions-to-three-targets cardinality mismatch are explicit in repository code. Magnitude depends on session count and fallback eligibility, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: central catalog/database reads, provider metadata round trips, session-database opens, and CPU over all registered sessions
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each move_session invocation performs work proportional to the complete registered session history, although argument resolution needs only the source, destination, and optional anchor; in the documented link-based flow this repeats the same full scan just performed by list_sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: The move tool's critical path gains avoidable I/O and latency, with fallback sessions adding one provider round trip plus session-database reads each and fallback concurrency limited to four.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, requesting list_sessions performed one full catalog computation and no subsequent move tool immediately forced another one; existing targeted session operations can use the accessor's getSession(session) lookup.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every move_session execution constructs a lookup backed by accessor.listSessions(). createMoveSessionLookup coalesces lookups only within that one call, while AgentService.listSessions retains results only while a computation is in flight and deletes settled entries, so a preceding list_sessions call is not reused.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new execute path at RIGHT line 413 unconditionally invokes the full listSessions accessor for move argument resolution; no equivalent post-list scan existed before the new tool.
Findings.Title: Avoid rescanning the entire session catalog for each move
Findings.Impact: The normal workflow tells the model to obtain links from list_sessions and then call move_session. On a large history, the second call blocks confirmation/move progress on another full catalog read; legacy/fallback rows can reopen per-session storage and contact providers before the requested move starts.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 413 wires argument resolution to `createMoveSessionLookup(() => accessor.listSessions())`. AgentService.listSessions removes settled computations from `_inFlightListSessions`; `_computeSessions` bulk-reads all catalog candidates and documents that each provider fallback costs a provider round trip plus session-database reads, under a Limiter(4). getMoveSessionArgs performs only source/destination/anchor resolution (at most three distinct sessions).
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve the at-most-three referenced sessions through targeted getSession/state-catalog lookups (including their recorded chats), or carry a generation-keyed short-lived listing from the immediately preceding list_sessions call; preserve freshness by revalidating the selected sessions in the existing move sequencer rather than recomputing the entire catalog.

Scenarios.Scenario: Broad list_sessions request, including the default move-disabled configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentService.listSessions must enumerate metadata, filter it, serialize every returned session, and hand the text to the provider's LLM tool-result channel before the agent can continue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Bulk-read catalog metadata for all eligible registered sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bulk operation spanning all registered candidates per settled list call
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same broad list already performed this catalog read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read provider/session metadata for catalog fallback rows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one provider metadata round trip plus session-database reads per fallback session, limited to four concurrent rows
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fallback existed before this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize nested chat title/link/status objects into the LLM tool result
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One object per visible nested chat across every returned session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only top-level session metadata was serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds synchronous allocation and increases provider/model result bytes

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All non-archived top-level sessions, plus after this diff all visible nested chats contained by them; there is no default result cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent list requests of the same mode coalesce only while a computation is in flight. Catalog fallback resolution uses Limiter(4); serialization is synchronous after metadata resolution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm eligible central catalog avoids per-session provider/session-db fallback, but still performs a central bulk read. Settled list computations are removed, so sequential calls recompute. Nested-chat serialization is repeated on every result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new all-chat map, uncapped broad filter, JSON serialization, and direct provider handoff are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Nested-chat history size varies; tens of nested chats are supported and persisted, but repository evidence does not establish percentile sizes or measured token latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: The payload grows with total nested chats even while move_session is disabled. This mechanism was investigated as serialization pressure; the concrete accepted review finding instead targets the more costly repeated full catalog scan on the move workflow.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move another nested session or whole session with move_session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After confirmation, argument resolution awaits a full listSessions computation; only then can the globally sequenced move restore selected sessions, read catalogs/worktree state, and commit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute the full session list to resolve at most three move references
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One all-session catalog computation per move invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No move tool forced a second full listing after links were obtained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly blocks every move before selected-session validation begins

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source/destination catalog snapshots and worktree ownership/session state for the selected move
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded per selected source/destination, with descendant chat-state reads proportional to the moved subtree
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing AHP/UI move paths used these operations, but the PR newly exposes them on this server-tool path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authoritative validation and commit block move completion

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source worktree records and destination primary-worktree metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source read, one destination primary read, and one detached-worktree read per additional worktree
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing moves performed these selected-session reads; the new tool invokes the same path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Argument resolution needs at most source, destination, and optional anchor, but the added lookup scans all registered sessions; move work additionally scales with the moved chat subtree and recorded worktrees.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All checks and moves use one global chat-move Sequencer. Full-list fallback rows run at concurrency four; the move itself does not overlap another move.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Lookups within one invocation share one listing promise, but no settled result is reused from the list_sessions call that normally supplied the links. Warm catalogs reduce fallback cost but not the all-session bulk read.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: line 413 unconditionally supplies listSessions, and the in-flight cache is deleted after settlement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Latency depends on total history and catalog fallback eligibility; the all-history cardinality mismatch is certain even when the warm bulk read is fast.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated work: the normal list_sessions-to-move_session sequence performs two sequential full catalog computations although move resolution references at most three sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move the calling chat after its turn succeeds
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool first performs the full-list lookup and a sequenced pre-check. Turn end then holds queued-chat admission while a second authoritative sequenced validation and move completes; queued messages cannot start before release.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full session-list computation for argument resolution
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the tool result and therefore turn completion

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Pre-check and later re-read catalog/chat/worktree state during authoritative apply
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two selected-move validation rounds for a successful self move; descendant reads scale with moved subtree
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing direct moves performed only their authoritative validation/apply round.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First round blocks scheduling; second blocks queued turns while admission is held

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Full registered session count for lookup; moved subtree size and worktree count for both pre-check and authoritative apply.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pre-check and apply serialize with all moves. The scheduled map holds at most one entry per chat/turn, and queued turns are explicitly held during apply.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The move lookup has only per-invocation coalescing. Pre-check state cannot safely serve as an authoritative cache because state may change before turn end; apply revalidates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the two validation rounds and admission hold; lower for material user impact beyond the list scan.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Moved subtrees are usually small and the duplicate validation is an intentional freshness tradeoff; no measurements show it dominates the already reported full-list scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: revalidation is required because the move is intentionally deferred until turn success, and caching the first result would violate freshness.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle chat.agentHost.moveChats.enabled and refresh advertised tools
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On the relevant setting transition, the host iterates loaded sessions, recomputes definitions, and dispatches a server-tools change only when definitions differ.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish SessionServerToolsChanged for each loaded session whose advertised catalog changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one dispatch per loaded session when this specific setting flips
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during the setting update, not startup or normal tool invocation

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently loaded sessions, not total persisted history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous serial iteration on a user-driven root configuration event; no burst limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The last enabled value is retained, so unrelated root config changes do only one configuration lookup and do not iterate/advertise. advertise compares definitions and suppresses unchanged dispatches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the value guard and per-loaded-session loop are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously loaded sessions is not established, but this is a rare explicit configuration transition.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not reportable: work is bounded to actual feature-setting transitions and is required to update tool availability.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 68 changed files' inventory and relevant production/test diffs. Submitted one high-confidence repeated-work finding for the uncached all-session scan on each move_session call. Also traced serialization growth, deferred-move revalidation, configuration fan-out, cache behavior, and database/provider/filesystem boundaries; no regression-fix learning record was warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
